ConnectionStrings.//: Dev/E2E only: the local Redis the README starts. It carries access-token and device revocations between hosts, so without it AUTH_TK_10 and DEV_REV_01 fail. Redis being down is not fatal (AbortOnConnectFail is off). Production sets ConnectionStrings__Redis in the environment.

SignUpChallenge.//: Dev/E2E only. The suite registers close to a thousand users, each solving the sign-up proof of work in the Api.Client, so the production default of 18 bits would add minutes. Still on, so every registration exercises it.

Authentication.//: Dev/E2E only. The limiter partitions on the caller's IP, and every E2E test shares one, so the production default of 10 a minute trips within the first few scenarios. The suite spends close to a thousand on its own (most scenarios register and sign in a user of their own), so the raised limit has to sit well clear of that, not just above it. The rate-limit scenarios restart this host with RateLimiting__Authentication__PermitLimit=10 (see Tests/Wbskt.E2E.FeatureTests/README.md). Production leaves this unset and gets the default.

TokenRefresh.//: Dev/E2E only, for the same reason. The refresh rate-limit scenario restarts this host with RateLimiting__TokenRefresh__PermitLimit=120.

SignUpChallenge.//: Dev/E2E only, for the same reason: every registration in the suite fetches a challenge.

EmailVerification.//: Dev/E2E only, for the same reason. The rate-limit scenarios restart this host with RateLimiting__EmailVerification__PermitLimit=10.

Api.//: Dev/E2E only. The limiter partitions on the signed-in user: the Auth scenarios all act as the seeded admin, and a scenario polling for a run's outcome calls faster than a person clicks. Production leaves this unset and gets the default (600 a minute, bursts of 120).
